title: Route Health Orchestra — dashboard spec for per-route & per-model operational signals
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Design a compact, prioritized operational dashboard — the 'Route Health Orchestra' — that surfaces per-route and per-model signals (latency distributions, throughput, token volume, error surfaces, and cost rate) for SREs and product engineers. This is intended as a top-level canvas for on-call and triage workflows: fast anomaly triage, root-cause breadcrumbs, and quick drilldowns into model variants and rollout lanes. Scope: one route-focused canvas and a companion per-model comparison view. Not in scope: long-term historical retention UI, billing invoices, or role-based access decisions (these are separate PM tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Canvas loads within 1s with default 7d time window on staging data
Charts include: latency distribution (P50/P90/P99), throughput sparkline, tokens-per-request waterfall, error-rate heatmap, and cost-rate microbar
Primary interaction patterns: time-window selector, model-variant toggle, route-filter, and quick-export to CSV
Inline drilldown: clicking a latency spike opens a microtrace swimlane and links to the most recent matching request sample
Design handoff assets (Figma + tokens + chart spec) delivered and reviewed by frontend and infra teams
Accessibility: color palette passes contrast AA for all semantic states
tasks: Finalize chart type decisions and aggregation windows
Prototype interactions in Figma (desktop & compact mobile) — include micro-interactions for hover and selection
Create chart specification doc with required fields, aggregation SQL examples, and recommended Vega-lite configs
Run review with ENG/PM on 2025-01-09 and capture action items
Prepare handoff package and record a 20-minute walkthrough video
comments: 2025-01-05 — Maya Chen: Initial wireframes uploaded to Figma. Focused on a prioritized signal lane in the top row and a timeline detail pane below.
2025-01-07 — Elliot Brooks: Iterated on the token waterfall to show tokens-per-step (prompt, model, post-process) and added a toggle for absolute vs normalized token counts.

2025-01-09 — Diego Rivera (ENG): Reviewed aggregation windows. Recommended 1m rollup for latency/throughput, 5m for token histograms in high-TPS routes. Blocker: backend needs an index for per-variant token stats (ENG-2312).
2025-01-09 — Priya Anand (PM): Requested a compact header that surfaces SLA status (green/amber/red) and the most recent rollout tag; also asked for a 'fast rollback' CTA placeholder for future work.
2025-01-10 — Accessibility review (Samir Patel): Color palette adjusted to meet AA; added patterned fills option for error heatmap for colorblind modes.
decisions: Choose distribution + percentile band (P50 median line, shaded P10–P90) for latency because it balances single-number clarity and distribution awareness.
Use a violin plot for per-model throughput distribution in the model-compare view to show skew on high-traffic routes.
Token waterfall split into 3 semantic buckets (prompt, model-inference, post-processing) to make optimization targets actionable.
Default time window set to 7d with quick presets (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d).
On missing metrics, surface a lightweight infobar with likely causes (ingest lag, disabled telemetry) and a link to the ingestion status dashboard.
tradeoffs: High-cardinality breakdowns (user, customer, session) are omitted from the default canvas to keep the load fast; these are available in the drilldown pane.
Choosing violin plots increases visual complexity for some viewers vs simple bar charts; we retain bar chart fallback in per-route compact mode.
Real-time 1s updates were deprioritized to avoid backend pressure; we expect 10s–30s refresh frequency for high-volume routes.
